description: Infographic arguing FISA redactions were illegal, headlined 'ARE THE FISA REDACTIONS LEGAL? DECLAS!'. It combines: a screenshot of a The Hill opinion article by John Solomon (10/07/18) claiming FBI redactions of 'Footnote 43' protected political embarrassment rather than national security; screenshots of three Q posts (No.363 of 10/08/18, No.239 of 09/15/18, No.260 of 09/18/18) citing the article and Executive Order 13526 Sec 1.7; and a screenshot of EO 13526 (signed by Barack Obama, Dec 29 2009) with clause (2) 'prevent embarrassment to a person, organization, or agency' highlighted and red lines connecting the panels. The compilation presents the article's and Q posts' claims that redactions concealed embarrassment; these are claims, not established fact.

And when, nine months later, the FBI could not prove the allegation of collusion between Trump and Russia, unverified evidence was leaked to the media to try to sustain public support for a continued investigation. So, Mr. President, when you weigh those DOJ/FBI arguments against declassification, please don't forget the ruse of the redaction that was Footnote 43. Part 1 - Original Classification. Part 2 - Derivative Classification. Part 3 - Declassification and Downgrading. Part 4 - Safeguarding. Part 5 - Implementation and Review. Part 6 - General Provisions. This order prescribes a uniform system for classifying, safeguarding, and declassifying national security information, including information relating to defense against transnational terrorism. Our democratic principles require that the American people be informed of the activities of their Government. Also, our Nation's progress depends on the free flow of information both within the Government and to the American people. Nevertheless, throughout our history, the national defense has required that certain information be maintained in confidence in order to protect our citizens, our democratic institutions, our homeland security, and our interactions with foreign nations. Protecting information critical to our Nation's security and demonstrating our commitment to open Government through accurate and accountable application of classification standards and routine, secure, and effective declassification are equally important priorities. description: Screenshot of a news article headline claiming a report that Google hid a user data breach from the public out of fear Congress would take action (referencing the 2018 Google+ data exposure). The accompanying AP photo by Jose Luis Magana shows an empty witness chair and table at a U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence hearing with a white 'GOOGLE' nameplate — the widely-circulated image of the seat Google left empty at the September 2018 hearing. Social share buttons (Facebook, email, Google+, Twitter) appear under the headline.
text: REPORT: GOOGLE HID USER DATA BREACH FROM PUBLIC OUT OF FEAR CONGRESS WOULD TAKE ACTION. SHARE 28. EMAIL. SHARE. TWEET. U.S. Senate Select Committee on INTELLIGENCE. GOOGLE. AP/Jose Luis Magana.
orgs: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
places: U.S. Senate hearing room, Washington D.C.
